items.text: Oil down sharply (WTI -7%, Brent -10% WoW) from geopolitical escalation, but price levels remain elevated; energy-driven inflation is forcing both ECB and Fed into sustained tightening despite moderating growth. Credit spreads widened YTD; energy-leveraged issuers and refinancing risk in levered energy remain structurally vulnerable.

CPI headline at 3.35% YoY (up from 3.30%), PPI accelerating to 5.41% YoY, and consumer inflation expectations spiking (one-year at 4.6%, up from 4.0% in August). ECB hiked deposit rate to 2.50% in September and futures price 58% odds of another 25bp by end-October. Sticky core inflation and wage anchors remain fragile; special situations credit faces refinancing cost pressures.

University of Michigan sentiment crashed to 48.1 in September (lowest in 4 months, down 15% YTD). Housing starts contracting (1,275k vs 1,309k prior), existing home sales down, mortgage rates at 7.03%. Consumer spending may slow; CRE and residential mortgage-backed credit face headwinds as affordability deteriorates and consumer confidence breaks.

Claims steady at 197k, but payroll gains weak (162k in August), unemployment holding at 4.1%. Average hourly earnings decelerating (3.09% from 3.24% YoY) and labor force participation remains soft. Wage growth is no longer catching up to inflation; risk of wage-led deflation in some pockets, but also persistent slack that may limit labor-intensive credit recovery.

ISM Manufacturing at 54.6 (August), down from 55.6, with order flows slowing sharply. China's official PMI at 49.8 in August, still in contraction. GDPNow tracker at 5.0%, but this may reflect data lag; underlying momentum cooling. Cyclical credit assets face demand headwinds; credit underwriters must distinguish high-beta growth stories from structural deterioration.

UST 10y at 5.18% (up 17bp WoW), 2y at 4.87%, yield curve normalizing (36bp vs 20bp prior). HY OAS widened to 280bp, CCC OAS to 1112bp. Fed holding at 4.0%, signaling pause, but inflation and ECB/global tightening keep real rates elevated. Credit spreads have repriced higher; illiquid / leveraged / refinancing-heavy names face acute pressure.

Middle East conflict driving energy shocks, trade tensions rising, ECB rates now 2.50% while Fed is on hold. Dollar strength, yuan weakness, and cross-border credit stress in EM corporates exposed to trade and FX volatility. Special-situations players should monitor distressed EM USD debt and trade finance dislocations.

themeCards.title: Energy Shock & Refinancing Risk
themeCards.statusLine: Middle East conflict driving WTI/Brent down from recent highs but sustaining elevated price floors. Energy inflation cascading into broader PPI and consumer expectations, forcing ECB to tighten despite slowing growth.
themeCards.relevance: Energy-linked leveraged issuers (exploration, midstream, integrated oils) refinancing into higher rate environment with elevated spreads. Commodity volatility creates distress opportunities in hedged/leveraged structures.

themeCards.title: Consumer Confidence Collapse & Real Incomes
themeCards.statusLine: University of Michigan sentiment fell to 48.1, lowest in 4 months and down 15% YTD. Inflation expectations (4.6% 1Y) and deteriorating business outlook driving broad-based household pessimism across political spectrum.
themeCards.relevance: Sentiment nadir signals demand risk for consumer-sensitive credit and CRE. Retail/restaurant levered balance sheets may face volume compression; discretionary spending credit faces term extension / restructuring risk if wage growth cannot close inflation gap.

themeCards.title: Housing Market Affordability Cliff
themeCards.statusLine: Mortgage rates at 7.03%, housing starts down to 1.275M, existing home sales fell to 3.98M SAAR. Affordability ratios at decade highs limiting buyer pools and reducing turnover.
themeCards.relevance: Builder credit (debt refinancing, land holdings, draw schedules) faces demand cliff. Residential MBS / non-agency RMBS credit quality deteriorating; mortgage servicing and default rates may inflect higher if labor market weakens further.

themeCards.title: Cross-Border & EM FX Dislocation
themeCards.statusLine: ECB at 2.50% while Fed paused at 4.0%; trade tensions rising; yuan weakness and dollar bid creating FX stress. EM corporates with USD debt facing valuation and cash-flow headwinds.
themeCards.relevance: Corporate EM credit in FX-exposed sectors (autos, tech, commodities) showing distress signals. Special situations players can identify debt exchanges, liability management events, and covenant-lite opportunites in EM multi-name portfolios with cross-currency exposure.

themeCards.title: Yield Curve Normalization & Refinancing Wall
themeCards.statusLine: 10y UST up to 5.18%, 2/10 curve steepened to +36bp. Floating-rate and near-term maturities face rising reset costs; 2026-2027 refinancing calendar increasingly pressure-tested.
themeCards.relevance: Large 2026-2027 refinancing wall (CLOs, ABS, corporates) coinciding with wider spreads and higher absolute rates. Opportunites in refinancing-challenged credits, covenant-lite loans, and extension trades where issuers lack alternative access.

regime.label: Late-cycle — stagflation precursor
regime.detail: Energy shock driving inflation expectations higher, consumer sentiment at decade lows, but labor market cooling and growth slowing; credit spreads widened sharply, refinancing risks acute, ECB hiking into weakness
